explanation: Die `EXCEPT` Klausel in `CORRESPONDING` ermöglicht es, bestimmte Felder von der Zuordnung auszuschließen. Dies ist nützlich, wenn die meisten Felder übereinstimmen, aber einige bewusst nicht kopiert werden sollen.
keywords: CORRESPONDING, EXCEPT, Structure Mapping

Instructions: Kopieren Sie Felder von einer Quellstruktur in eine Zielstruktur, wobei vorhandene Werte in der Zielstruktur für bestimmte Felder beibehalten werden.
hint: Verwenden Sie `CORRESPONDING` mit der `KEEPING` Klausel.
solution:
CLASS zcl_cor_keeping DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION:
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_source,
             field1 TYPE string,
             field2 TYPE i,
             field3 TYPE string,
           END OF ty_source,
           BEGIN OF ty_target,
             field1 TYPE string,
             field2 TYPE i,
             field3 TYPE string,
           END OF ty_target.
    METHODS map_keeping
      IMPORTING
        is_source TYPE ty_source
        is_base   TYPE ty_target
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rs_target) TYPE ty_target.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_cor_keeping IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD map_keeping.
    rs_target = CORRESPONDING #( BASE ( is_base )
                                 FROM is_source
                                 KEEPING field2 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION:
    METHODS test_map_keeping FOR TESTING.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_map_keeping.
    DATA(ls_source) = VALUE zcl_cor_keeping=>ty_source( field1 = 'New A' field2 = 999 field3 = 'New C' ).
    DATA(ls_base) = VALUE zcl_cor_keeping=>ty_target( field1 = 'Old A' field2 = 123 field3 = 'Old C' ).
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_cor_keeping( ).

explanation: Die `KEEPING` Klausel in `CORRESPONDING` stellt sicher, dass die Werte der angegebenen Felder aus der `BASE`-Struktur beibehalten und nicht von der Quellstruktur überschrieben werden.
keywords: CORRESPONDING, KEEPING, Structure Mapping

Instructions: Mappen Sie eine interne Tabelle mit verschachtelten Strukturen und Tabellen auf eine andere.
hint: `CORRESPONDING` unterstützt auch verschachtelte Strukturen und Tabellen. Verwenden Sie die hierarchische `MAPPING` Syntax.
solution:
CLASS zcl_cor_nested DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION:
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_item_source,
             item_id TYPE i,
             item_name TYPE string,
           END OF ty_item_source,
           ty_items_source TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_item_source WITH EMPTY KEY,
           BEGIN OF ty_header_source,
             doc_id TYPE i,
             doc_date TYPE d,
             items TYPE ty_items_source,
           END OF ty_header_source,
           ty_headers_source TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_header_source WITH EMPTY KEY,

           BEGIN OF ty_item_target,
             position TYPE i,
             product_name TYPE string,
           END OF ty_item_target,
           ty_items_target TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_item_target WITH EMPTY KEY,
           BEGIN OF ty_header_target,
             document_number TYPE i,
             document_date TYPE d,
             positions TYPE ty_items_target,
           END OF ty_header_target,
           ty_headers_target TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_header_target WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS map_nested_tables
      IMPORTING
        it_source TYPE ty_headers_source
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_target) TYPE ty_headers_target.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_cor_nested IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD map_nested_tables.
    rt_target = CORRESPONDING #( BASE ( VALUE ty_headers_target( ) )
                                 FROM it_source
                                 MAPPING document_number = doc_id
                                         document_date = doc_date
                                         positions = items
                                         ( position = item_id
                                           product_name = item_name ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION:
    METHODS test_map_nested FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_map_nested.
    DATA(lt_source) = VALUE zcl_cor_nested=>ty_headers_source(
      ( doc_id = 100 doc_date = '20231211'
        items = VALUE #(
          ( item_id = 1 item_name = 'Laptop' )
          ( item_id = 2 item_name = 'Mouse' )
        )
      )
    ).
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_cor_nested( ).
    DATA(lt_target) = lo_cut->map_nested_tables( lt_source ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_target ) exp = 1 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-document_number exp = 100 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-document_date exp = '20231211' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_target[ 1 ]-positions ) exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-positions[ 1 ]-position exp = 1 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-positions[ 1 ]-product_name exp = 'Laptop' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: `CORRESPONDING` kann auch für komplexe Datenstrukturen mit verschachtelten Tabellen und Strukturen verwendet werden. Die `MAPPING` Klausel wird hier hierarchisch angewendet, um die Zuordnung auf allen Ebenen zu steuern.
keywords: CORRESPONDING, Nested Tables, Mapping, Deep Structure

Instructions: Ermitteln Sie den aktuell aktiven UI5-Theme-Namen im Backend.
hint: Verwenden Sie die statische Methode `GET_ACTIVE_THEME` der Klasse `/UI5/CL_THEME_UTIL`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_ui5_get_theme DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION:
    METHODS get_current_ui5_theme
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_theme_name) TYPE /ui5/theme_name.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_ui5_get_theme IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_current_ui5_theme.
    " In einem realen Szenario würde dies typischerweise innerhalb eines UI5-Kontextes
    " oder dort aufgerufen, wo das Theme explizit gesetzt/bekannt ist.
    " Für die Demonstration simulieren wir einen Standardwert oder rufen ihn aus einem Kontext ab.
    " Das tatsächlich aktive Theme hängt von den Benutzereinstellungen und dem Anwendungskontext ab.
    " Hier nehmen wir einen Standardwert oder ein global konfiguriertes Theme an.
    " Für einen echten Laufzeitwert sind oft HTTP-Kontext oder Benutzerstandards involviert.
    TRY.

Instructions: Erstellen Sie einen formatierten String aus einer Liste von Werten, wobei jeder Wert in Großbuchstaben umgewandelt wird und durch Kommas getrennt ist.
hint: Verwenden Sie String Templates in Kombination mit `FOR` und `REDUCE`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_str_template_for_red DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION:
    METHODS format_list_to_string
      IMPORTING
        it_values TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF string WITH EMPTY KEY
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_formatted_string) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_str_template_for_red IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD format_list_to_string.
    rv_formatted_string = REDUCE string(
      INIT result = ``
      FOR value IN it_values
      NEXT result = COND string( WHEN result IS INITIAL THEN |{ to_upper( value ) }|
                                 ELSE |{ result }, { to_upper( value ) }| )
    ).
    rv_formatted_string = |Formatted List: { rv_formatted_string }|.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION:
    METHODS test_format_list FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_format_list.
    DATA(lt_values) = VALUE STANDARD TABLE OF string WITH EMPTY KEY(
      ( 'apple' )
      ( 'banana' )
      ( 'cherry' )
    ).
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_str_template_for_red( ).
    DATA(lv_result) = lo_cut->format_list_to_string( lt_values ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_result exp = 'Formatted List: APPLE, BANANA, CHERRY' ).

    DATA(lt_empty_values) = VALUE STANDARD TABLE OF string WITH EMPTY KEY( ).
    DATA(lv_empty_result) = lo_cut->format_list_to_string( lt_empty_values ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_empty_result exp = 'Formatted List: ' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel nutzt String Templates in Kombination mit `REDUCE` und `FOR`, um eine Liste von Strings zu aggregieren und zu formatieren. `REDUCE` ist ideal für die iterative Erstellung eines einzelnen Ergebnisses, während `FOR` die Schleife über die interne Tabelle vereinfacht. `to_upper` ist eine eingebaute Funktion für die Großschreibung.
keywords: String Templates, FOR, REDUCE, Internal Tables, Functional Programming

Instructions: Filtern Sie eine interne Tabelle basierend auf einem Kriterium.

CLASS zcl_filter_table DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data_line,

CLASS zcl_filter_table IMPLEMENTATION.

Instructions: Mappen Sie eine interne Tabelle auf eine andere, wobei nur bestimmte Felder kopiert werden und andere ignoriert werden.
hint: Verwenden Sie `CORRESPONDING` mit einer Kombination aus `MAPPING` und implizitem Ignorieren.
solution:
CLASS zcl_cor_selective_map DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION:
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_source_line,
             key_field TYPE string,
             data_field1 TYPE i,
             data_field2 TYPE string,
             ignore_field TYPE d,
           END OF ty_source_line,
           ty_source_table TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_source_line WITH EMPTY KEY,
           BEGIN OF ty_target_line,
             id_key TYPE string,
             value1 TYPE i,
             value2 TYPE string,
             status TYPE c LENGTH 1,
           END OF ty_target_line,
           ty_target_table TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_target_line WITH EMPTY KEY.
    METHODS map_selective_fields
      IMPORTING
        it_source TYPE ty_source_table
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_target) TYPE ty_target_table.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_cor_selective_map IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD map_selective_fields.
    rt_target = CORRESPONDING #( BASE ( VALUE ty_target_table( ) )
                                 FROM it_source
                                 MAPPING id_key = key_field
                                         value1 = data_field1
                                         value2 = data_field2 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION:
    METHODS test_selective_mapping FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_selective_mapping.
    DATA(lt_source) = VALUE zcl_cor_selective_map=>ty_source_table(
      ( key_field = 'K1' data_field1 = 10 data_field2 = 'Text A' ignore_field = '20230101' )
      ( key_field = 'K2' data_field1 = 20 data_field2 = 'Text B' ignore_field = '20230201' )
    ).
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_cor_selective_map( ).
    DATA(lt_target) = lo_cut->map_selective_fields( lt_source ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_target ) exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-id_key exp = 'K1' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-value1 exp = 10 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-value2 exp = 'Text A' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( lt_target[ 1 ]-status ). " status sollte initial sein
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel zeigt, wie `CORRESPONDING` mit `MAPPING` verwendet werden kann, um nur eine Teilmenge von Feldern von einer Quelltabelle in eine Zieltabelle zu kopieren. Felder, die nicht in der `MAPPING`-Klausel aufgeführt sind und keine Namensübereinstimmung haben, werden ignoriert.
keywords: CORRESPONDING, Internal Table, Selective Mapping, MAPPING

Instructions: Mappen Sie eine interne Tabelle auf eine andere, wobei ein Feld basierend auf einer Bedingung transformiert wird.
hint: Verwenden Sie `CORRESPONDING` mit `MAPPING` und einer `COND` Ausdruck.
solution:
CLASS zcl_cor_cond_map DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION:
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_source_line,
             id     TYPE i,
             value  TYPE i,
           END OF ty_source_line,
           ty_source_table TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_source_line WITH EMPTY KEY,
           BEGIN OF ty_target_line,
             item_id TYPE i,
             status  TYPE string,
           END OF ty_target_line,
           ty_target_table TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_target_line WITH EMPTY KEY.
    METHODS map_with_condition
      IMPORTING
        it_source TYPE ty_source_table
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_target) TYPE ty_target_table.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_cor_cond_map IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD map_with_condition.
    rt_target = CORRESPONDING #( BASE ( VALUE ty_target_table( ) )
                                 FROM it_source
                                 MAPPING item_id = id
                                         status = COND string( WHEN value > 100 THEN 'HIGH' ELSE 'LOW' ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION:
    METHODS test_map_with_condition FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_map_with_condition.
    DATA(lt_source) = VALUE zcl_cor_cond_map=>ty_source_table(
      ( id = 1 value = 50 )
      ( id = 2 value = 150 )
      ( id = 3 value = 100 )
    ).
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_cor_cond_map( ).
    DATA(lt_target) = lo_cut->map_with_condition( lt_source ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_target ) exp = 3 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-item_id exp = 1 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-status exp = 'LOW' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 2 ]-item_id exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 2 ]-status exp = 'HIGH' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 3 ]-item_id exp = 3 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 3 ]-status exp = 'LOW' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel demonstriert die Verwendung eines `COND`-Ausdrucks innerhalb der `MAPPING`-Klausel von `CORRESPONDING`. Dies ermöglicht die bedingte Zuweisung von Werten zu Zielfeldern basierend auf den Werten der Quellfelder, was zu sehr kompaktem und ausdrucksstarkem Code führt.
keywords: CORRESPONDING, Internal Table, Conditional Mapping, MAPPING, COND

Instructions: Löschen Sie alle Flüge aus einer internen Tabelle, bei denen die Fluggesellschaft 'AA' und die Flugnummer '0017' ist, unter Verwendung eines FILTER-Ausdrucks.
hint: Nutzen Sie den DELETE-Befehl in Kombination mit einem FILTER-Ausdruck, um die zu löschenden Zeilen zu identifizieren.
solution:
CLASS zcl_delete_filter DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             price    TYPE sflight-price,
           END OF ty_sflight.
    TYPES tt_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS delete_flights_by_filter
      IMPORTING
        it_flights TYPE tt_sflight
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_filtered_flights) TYPE tt_sflight.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_delete_filter IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD delete_flights_by_filter.
    rt_filtered_flights = FILTER #( it_flights EXCEPT IN it_flights WHERE carrid = 'AA' AND connid = '0017' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_delete_filter FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_delete_filter.
    DATA: lt_flights TYPE zcl_delete_filter=>tt_sflight.
    APPEND INITIAL LINE TO lt_flights ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_flight>).
    <fs_flight>-carrid = 'AA'.
    <fs_flight>-connid = '0017'.
    <fs_flight>-fldate = sy-datum.
    <fs_flight>-price = '100'.

    APPEND INITIAL LINE TO lt_flights ASSIGNING <fs_flight>.
    <fs_flight>-carrid = 'LH'.
    <fs_flight>-connid = '0400'.
    <fs_flight>-fldate = sy-datum.
    <fs_flight>-price = '200'.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_delete_filter( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->delete_flights_by_filter( lt_flights ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_result )
      exp = 1
      msg = 'Expected 1 flight after deletion'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_result[ 1 ]-carrid
      exp = 'LH'
      msg = 'Expected LH flight to remain'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der FILTER-Ausdruck ist eine moderne und funktionale Art, eine neue interne Tabelle zu erstellen, die nur die gewünschten Zeilen enthält. Anstatt Zeilen explizit zu löschen, wird hier eine neue Tabelle mit den verbleibenden Zeilen erzeugt, was oft effizienter und lesbarer ist.
keywords: DELETE, FILTER, Internal Tables, Functional Programming

Instructions: Löschen Sie aufeinanderfolgende Duplikate aus einer internen Tabelle basierend auf dem Feld 'CARRID'.
hint: Verwenden Sie den Befehl DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM itab COMPARING field.
solution:
CLASS zcl_delete_adj_dup DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             key_field TYPE c LENGTH 10,
             value     TYPE i,
           END OF ty_data.
    TYPES tt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS delete_adjacent_duplicates
      IMPORTING
        it_data TYPE tt_data
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_unique_data) TYPE tt_data.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_delete_adj_dup IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD delete_adjacent_duplicates.
    rt_unique_data = it_data.
    SORT rt_unique_data BY key_field. " Sorting is crucial for ADJACENT DUPLICATES
    DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM rt_unique_data COMPARING key_field.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_delete_adjacent_duplicates FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_delete_adjacent_duplicates.
    DATA: lt_test_data TYPE zcl_delete_adj_dup=>tt_data.
    APPEND VALUE #( key_field = 'A' value = 1 ) TO lt_test_data.
    APPEND VALUE #( key_field = 'A' value = 2 ) TO lt_test_data.
    APPEND VALUE #( key_field = 'B' value = 3 ) TO lt_test_data.
    APPEND VALUE #( key_field = 'A' value = 4 ) TO lt_test_data. " This 'A' should remain after sorting and deleting
    APPEND VALUE #( key_field = 'B' value = 5 ) TO lt_test_data.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_delete_adj_dup( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->delete_adjacent_duplicates( lt_test_data ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_result )
      exp = 2 " Expected: A, B (after sorting and deleting adjacent)
      msg = 'Expected 2 unique entries after deleting adjacent duplicates'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_result[ 1 ]-key_field
      exp = 'A'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_result[ 2 ]-key_field
      exp = 'B'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der Befehl DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES ist eine effiziente Möglichkeit, doppelte Zeilen, die direkt aufeinanderfolgen, aus einer internen Tabelle zu entfernen. Es ist wichtig, die Tabelle vorher nach dem Vergleichsfeld zu sortieren, um alle Duplikate zu erfassen.
keywords: DELETE, ADJACENT DUPLICATES, Internal Tables, Sorting

Instructions: Parsen Sie einen CSV-String in eine interne Tabelle unter Verwendung der Klasse CL_ICF_CSV.

CLASS zcl_csv_parser DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.

    METHODS parse_csv_string
      IMPORTING
        iv_csv_string TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_data) TYPE tt_sflight_csv
      RAISING
        cx_sy_conversion_error.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_csv_parser IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD parse_csv_string.
    DATA(lo_csv_parser) = cl_icf_csv=>create_from_string(
                             i_content = iv_csv_string
                             i_separator = ','
                             i_has_header = abap_true
                           ).
    lo_csv_parser->parse(
      IMPORTING
        e_table = rt_data
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_parse_csv FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_parse_csv_error FOR TESTING RAISING cx_static_check.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_parse_csv.
    DATA(lv_csv_data) = 'CARRID,CONNID,FLDATE' && cl_abap_char_utilities=>cr_lf &&
                        'AA,0017,20251211' && cl_abap_char_utilities=>cr_lf &&
                        'LH,0400,20251212'.

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_result )
      exp = 2

Instructions: Demonstrieren Sie die Fehlerbehandlung beim Parsen eines ungültigen CSV-Strings unter Verwendung der Klasse CL_ICF_CSV.
hint: Verwenden Sie TRY...CATCH-Blöcke, um Ausnahmen wie CX_SY_CONVERSION_ERROR abzufangen.
solution:
CLASS zcl_csv_error_handling DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             id TYPE i,
             value TYPE string,
           END OF ty_data.
    TYPES tt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS parse_csv_with_error_handling
      IMPORTING
        iv_csv_string TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_data) TYPE tt_data
      EXCEPTIONS
        parsing_failed.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_csv_error_handling IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD parse_csv_with_error_handling.
    TRY.
        DATA(lo_csv_parser) = cl_icf_csv=>create_from_string(
                                 i_content = iv_csv_string
                                 i_separator = ','
                                 i_has_header = abap_true
                               ).
        lo_csv_parser->parse(
          IMPORTING
            e_table = rt_data
        ).
      CATCH cx_sy_conversion_error INTO DATA(lx_conv_error).
        " Log error or handle specifically
        RAISE EXCEPTION TYPE zcx_csv_parsing_error " Custom exception for better context
          EXPORTING
            textid = zcx_csv_parsing_error=>parsing_failed
            previous = lx_conv_error.
      CATCH cx_sy_read_error INTO DATA(lx_read_error).
        RAISE EXCEPTION TYPE zcx_csv_parsing_error
          EXPORTING
            textid = zcx_csv_parsing_error=>read_error
            previous = lx_read_error.
      CATCH cx_root INTO DATA(lx_root).
        " Catch any other unexpected errors
        RAISE EXCEPTION TYPE zcx_csv_parsing_error
          EXPORTING
            textid = zcx_csv_parsing_error=>unknown_error
            previous = lx_root.
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine neue interne Tabelle, die nur eindeutige Fluggesellschaften (CARRID) aus einer SFLIGHTS-Tabelle enthält, unter Verwendung des REDUCE-Operators.
hint: Nutzen Sie REDUCE, um eine neue Tabelle aufzubauen und dabei Duplikate zu vermeiden, indem Sie COND und LINE_EXISTS verwenden.
solution:
CLASS zcl_reduce_unique DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_carrid,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
           END OF ty_carrid.
    TYPES tt_carrid TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_carrid WITH EMPTY KEY.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
           END OF ty_sflight.
    TYPES tt_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_unique_carriers
      IMPORTING
        it_flights TYPE tt_sflight
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_unique_carriers) TYPE tt_carrid.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_reduce_unique IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_unique_carriers.
    rt_unique_carriers = REDUCE tt_carrid(
      INIT result = VALUE tt_carrid( )
      FOR flight IN it_flights
      NEXT
        result = COND tt_carrid(
          WHEN line_exists( result[ carrid = flight-carrid ] ) THEN result
          ELSE VALUE tt_carrid( BASE result ( carrid = flight-carrid ) )
        )
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:

    APPEND VALUE #( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0400' fldate = sy-datum ) TO lt_flights.
    APPEND VALUE #( carrid = 'AA' connid = '0018' fldate = sy-datum ) TO lt_flights.
    APPEND VALUE #( carrid = 'UA' connid = '0001' fldate = sy-datum ) TO lt_flights.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_reduce_unique( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->get_unique_carriers( lt_flights ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_result )
      exp = 3
      msg = 'Expected 3 unique carriers'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_result[ 1 ]-carrid
      exp = 'AA'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_result[ 2 ]-carrid
      exp = 'LH'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_result[ 3 ]-carrid
      exp = 'UA'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_empty_table.
    DATA: lt_flights TYPE zcl_reduce_unique=>tt_sflight.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_reduce_unique( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->get_unique_carriers( lt_flights ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial(
      act = lines( lt_result )
      msg = 'Expected empty table for empty input'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der REDUCE-Operator ermöglicht die Aggregation von Daten aus einer internen Tabelle in ein einzelnes Ergebnis oder eine neue Tabelle. In diesem Beispiel wird er verwendet, um eine neue Tabelle mit eindeutigen Fluggesellschaften zu erstellen.              carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,

             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             price    TYPE sflight-price,
           END OF ty_sflight.
    TYPES tt_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS delete_flights_conditionally
      IMPORTING
        it_flights TYPE tt_sflight
        iv_carrid_to_keep TYPE sflight-carrid
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_remaining_flights) TYPE tt_sflight.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_delete_for_where IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD delete_flights_conditionally.
    rt_remaining_flights = VALUE #( 
      FOR flight IN it_flights WHERE ( carrid = iv_carrid_to_keep )
      ( flight )
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.

    APPEND VALUE #( carrid = 'AA' connid = '0017' fldate = sy-datum price = '100' ) TO lt_flights.
    APPEND VALUE #( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0400' fldate = sy-datum price = '200' ) TO lt_flights.

explanation: Anstatt Zeilen explizit zu löschen, ist es in modernem ABAP oft vorteilhafter, eine neue Tabelle mit den gewünschten Zeilen zu erstellen. Der VALUE-Operator in Verbindung mit einem FOR-Ausdruck und einer WHERE-Bedingung bietet eine sehr lesbare und effiziente Möglichkeit, dies zu erreichen, indem nur die Zeilen kopiert werden, die die angegebene Bedingung erfüllen.
keywords: DELETE, FOR, WHERE, VALUE, Internal Tables, Functional Programming

Instructions: Generieren Sie einen CSV-String aus einer internen Tabelle und schließen Sie dabei bestimmte Felder von der Ausgabe aus, unter Verwendung der Klasse CL_ICF_CSV.
hint: Verwenden Sie CL_ICF_CSV=>CREATE_FROM_TABLE und passen Sie die Struktur der internen Tabelle an, um unerwünschte Felder zu entfernen, oder nutzen Sie eine Mapping-Funktion, falls verfügbar.
solution:
CLASS zcl_csv_exclude_fields DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_full,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             price    TYPE sflight-price,
           END OF ty_sflight_full.
    TYPES tt_sflight_full TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight_full WITH EMPTY KEY.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_reduced,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
           END OF ty_sflight_reduced.
    TYPES tt_sflight_reduced TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight_reduced WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS generate_csv_excluding_fields
      IMPORTING
        it_data TYPE tt_sflight_full
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_csv_string) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_csv_exclude_fields IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD generate_csv_excluding_fields.
    " Create a new internal table with only the desired fields
    DATA(lt_reduced_data) = VALUE tt_sflight_reduced(
      FOR flight IN it_data
      ( CORRESPONDING #( flight ) )
    ).

    DATA(lo_csv_generator) = cl_icf_csv=>create_from_table(
                               i_table = lt_reduced_data
                               i_separator = ','
                               i_has_header = abap_true
                             ).
    rv_csv_string = lo_csv_generator->get_string( ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_exclude_fields FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_exclude_fields.
    DATA: lt_test_data TYPE zcl_csv_exclude_fields=>tt_sflight_full.
    APPEND VALUE #( carrid = 'AA' connid = '0017' fldate = '20251211' price = '100' ) TO lt_test_data.
    APPEND VALUE #( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0400' fldate = '20251212' price = '200' ) TO lt_test_data.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_csv_exclude_fields( ).
    DATA(lv_csv_result) = lo_cut->generate_csv_excluding_fields( lt_test_data ).

    DATA(lv_expected_csv) = 'CARRID,CONNID' && cl_abap_char_utilities=>cr_lf &&
                            'AA,0017' && cl_abap_char_utilities=>cr_lf &&
                            'LH,0400'.

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lv_csv_result
      exp = lv_expected_csv
      msg = 'Generated CSV string should exclude FLDATE and PRICE'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Um bestimmte Felder beim Generieren eines CSV-Strings auszuschließen, kann man eine Zwischen-Tabelle mit einer reduzierten Struktur erstellen. Der CORRESPONDING-Operator (ABAP 7.40+) in Kombination mit dem VALUE-Operator (ABAP 7.50+) ermöglicht eine prägnante und effiziente Feldzuordnung, wodurch nur die gewünschten Felder in die CSV-Ausgabe gelangen.
keywords: CL_ICF_CSV, CSV, Exclude Fields, CORRESPONDING, VALUE, Internal Tables

Instructions: Löschen Sie alle Zeilen aus einer internen Tabelle, die eine bestimmte Bedingung erfüllen, und geben Sie die gelöschten Zeilen zurück, unter Verwendung von FOR ... IN ... THEN ... ELSE.
hint: Nutzen Sie den VALUE-Operator mit einem FOR-Ausdruck und der THEN/ELSE-Syntax, um die Tabelle zu filtern und gleichzeitig die gelöschten Elemente zu erfassen.
solution:
CLASS zcl_delete_and_return DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             id TYPE i,
             value TYPE string,
           END OF ty_data.
    TYPES tt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS delete_and_get_deleted
      IMPORTING
        it_original_data TYPE tt_data
        iv_id_to_delete  TYPE i
      EXPORTING
        et_deleted_data  TYPE tt_data
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_remaining_data) TYPE tt_data.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_delete_and_return IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD delete_and_get_deleted.
    rt_remaining_data = VALUE tt_data(
      FOR entry IN it_original_data
      WHERE ( id <> iv_id_to_delete )
      ( entry )
    ).

    et_deleted_data = VALUE tt_data(
      FOR entry IN it_original_data
      WHERE ( id = iv_id_to_delete )
      ( entry )
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_delete_and_return FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_no_deletion FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_delete_and_return.
    DATA: lt_original TYPE zcl_delete_and_return=>tt_data.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 1 value = 'A' ) TO lt_original.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 2 value = 'B' ) TO lt_original.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 3 value = 'C' ) TO lt_original.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_delete_and_return( ).
    DATA(lt_deleted) = lo_cut->delete_and_get_deleted(
                            it_original_data = lt_original
                            iv_id_to_delete  = 2
                            EXPORTING
                              et_deleted_data = DATA(lt_exported_deleted)
                          ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_deleted )
      exp = 2
      msg = 'Expected 2 remaining entries'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_deleted[ 1 ]-id
      exp = 1
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_exported_deleted )
      exp = 1
      msg = 'Expected 1 deleted entry'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_exported_deleted[ 1 ]-id
      exp = 2
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_no_deletion.
    DATA: lt_original TYPE zcl_delete_and_return=>tt_data.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 1 value = 'A' ) TO lt_original.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_delete_and_return( ).
    DATA(lt_deleted) = lo_cut->delete_and_get_deleted(
                            it_original_data = lt_original
                            iv_id_to_delete  = 99
                            EXPORTING
                              et_deleted_data = DATA(lt_exported_deleted)
                          ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_deleted )
      exp = 1
      msg = 'Expected 1 remaining entry'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial(
      act = lines( lt_exported_deleted )
      msg = 'Expected no deleted entries'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Diese Methode demonstriert eine funktionale Art, Elemente aus einer Tabelle zu 'löschen' und gleichzeitig die gelöschten Elemente zu erfassen. Durch die Verwendung von zwei separaten VALUE-Ausdrücken mit FOR und WHERE-Bedingungen können sowohl die verbleibenden als auch die 'gelöschten' Elemente in neuen Tabellen gesammelt werden, was die Datenintegrität des Originals bewahrt und die Nachverfolgung erleichtert.
keywords: DELETE, VALUE, FOR, WHERE, Internal Tables, Functional Programming, ABAP 7.55

Instructions: Parsen Sie einen CSV-String, der leere Zeilen enthalten kann, und ignorieren Sie diese leeren Zeilen während des Parsens mit CL_ICF_CSV.
hint: Die Klasse CL_ICF_CSV behandelt leere Zeilen standardmäßig. Der Fokus liegt hier auf der Demonstration dieses Verhaltens und der Robustheit.
solution:
CLASS zcl_csv_ignore_empty DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             col1 TYPE string,
             col2 TYPE string,
           END OF ty_data.
    TYPES tt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS parse_csv_ignoring_empty_lines
      IMPORTING
        iv_csv_string TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_parsed_data) TYPE tt_data
      RAISING
        cx_sy_conversion_error.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_csv_ignore_empty IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD parse_csv_ignoring_empty_lines.
    DATA(lo_csv_parser) = cl_icf_csv=>create_from_string(
                             i_content = iv_csv_string
                             i_separator = ','
                             i_has_header = abap_true
                           ).
    lo_csv_parser->parse(
      IMPORTING
        e_table = rt_parsed_data
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_csv_with_empty_lines FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_only_empty_lines FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_csv_with_empty_lines.
    DATA(lv_csv_data) = 'Col1,Col2' && cl_abap_char_utilities=>cr_lf &&
                        'Val1,Val2' && cl_abap_char_utilities=>cr_lf &&
                        '' && cl_abap_char_utilities=>cr_lf && " Empty line
                        'Val3,Val4' && cl_abap_char_utilities=>cr_lf &&
                        ''. " Another empty line

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_csv_ignore_empty( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->parse_csv_ignoring_empty_lines( lv_csv_data ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_result )
      exp = 2
      msg = 'Expected 2 data rows, empty lines should be ignored'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_result[ 1 ]-col1
      exp = 'Val1'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_result[ 2 ]-col2
      exp = 'Val4'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_only_empty_lines.
    DATA(lv_csv_data) = 'Col1,Col2' && cl_abap_char_utilities=>cr_lf &&
                        '' && cl_abap_char_utilities=>cr_lf &&
                        ''.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_csv_ignore_empty( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->parse_csv_ignoring_empty_lines( lv_csv_data ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial(
      act = lines( lt_result )
      msg = 'Expected empty table when only empty lines are present after header'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die Klasse CL_ICF_CSV ist robust gegenüber leeren Zeilen in der Eingabe. Sie ignoriert diese standardmäßig, was die Verarbeitung von unsauberen CSV-Dateien vereinfacht. Dies ist ein Beispiel für die eingebaute Resilienz der Klasse, die Entwicklern hilft, weniger manuellen Bereinigungscode schreiben zu müssen.
keywords: CL_ICF_CSV, CSV, Empty Lines, Parsing, Robustness

Instructions: Löschen Sie alle Zeilen aus einer internen Tabelle, die in einer anderen internen Tabelle als Referenz vorhanden sind (Mengenoperation).
hint: Verwenden Sie den FILTER-Ausdruck mit EXCEPT IN, um Zeilen zu entfernen, die in einer Referenztabelle vorhanden sind.
solution:
CLASS zcl_delete_except_in DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_key,
             id TYPE i,
           END OF ty_key.
    TYPES tt_key TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_key WITH UNIQUE KEY id.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             id TYPE i,
             value TYPE string,
           END OF ty_data.
    TYPES tt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS delete_matching_keys
      IMPORTING
        it_original_data TYPE tt_data
        it_keys_to_delete TYPE tt_key
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_remaining_data) TYPE tt_data.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_delete_except_in IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD delete_matching_keys.
    rt_remaining_data = FILTER #( it_original_data EXCEPT IN it_keys_to_delete WHERE id = id ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_delete_matching_keys FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_no_matches_to_delete FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_delete_all_matches FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_delete_matching_keys.
    DATA: lt_original TYPE zcl_delete_except_in=>tt_data.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 1 value = 'A' ) TO lt_original.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 2 value = 'B' ) TO lt_original.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 3 value = 'C' ) TO lt_original.

    DATA: lt_keys_to_delete TYPE zcl_delete_except_in=>tt_key.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 2 ) TO lt_keys_to_delete.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_delete_except_in( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->delete_matching_keys(
                            it_original_data = lt_original
                            it_keys_to_delete = lt_keys_to_delete
                          ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_result )
      exp = 2
      msg = 'Expected 2 remaining entries'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_result[ 1 ]-id
      exp = 1
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lt_result[ 2 ]-id
      exp = 3
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_no_matches_to_delete.
    DATA: lt_original TYPE zcl_delete_except_in=>tt_data.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 1 value = 'A' ) TO lt_original.

    DATA: lt_keys_to_delete TYPE zcl_delete_except_in=>tt_key.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 99 ) TO lt_keys_to_delete.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_delete_except_in( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->delete_matching_keys(
                            it_original_data = lt_original
                            it_keys_to_delete = lt_keys_to_delete
                          ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lines( lt_result )
      exp = 1
      msg = 'Expected 1 remaining entry (no matches to delete)'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_delete_all_matches.
    DATA: lt_original TYPE zcl_delete_except_in=>tt_data.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 1 value = 'A' ) TO lt_original.

    DATA: lt_keys_to_delete TYPE zcl_delete_except_in=>tt_key.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 1 ) TO lt_keys_to_delete.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_delete_except_in( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->delete_matching_keys(
                            it_original_data = lt_original
                            it_keys_to_delete = lt_keys_to_delete
                          ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial(
      act = lines( lt_result )
      msg = 'Expected empty table (all matches deleted)'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der FILTER-Ausdruck mit der EXCEPT IN-Klausel ist eine leistungsstarke und moderne Möglichkeit, Mengenoperationen auf internen Tabellen durchzuführen. Er ermöglicht es, alle Zeilen aus einer Tabelle zu entfernen, deren Schlüssel in einer anderen Referenztabelle vorhanden sind, was eine deklarative und effiziente Alternative zu Schleifen und expliziten DELETE-Anweisungen darstellt.
keywords: DELETE, FILTER, EXCEPT IN, Internal Tables, Set Operations, Functional Programming

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine neue interne Tabelle, die nur die Flugnummern und die maximale Kapazität der SFLIGHTS-Tabelle enthält, wobei die Kapazität verdoppelt wird.
hint: Verwenden Sie den `FOR`-Operator, um eine neue Tabelle zu konstruieren.
solution:
CLASS zcl_itb_for_transform DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_capacity,
             carrid   TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid   TYPE s_conn_id,
             capacity TYPE i,
           END OF ty_flight_capacity.
    TYPES tt_flight_capacity TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_capacity WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_doubled_capacity
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_flights) TYPE tt_flight_capacity.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_itb_for_transform IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_doubled_capacity.
    SELECT carrid, connid, seatsmax FROM sflights INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_sflights).

    rt_flights = VALUE #( FOR ls_sflight IN lt_sflights
                          ( carrid   = ls_sflight-carrid
                            connid   = ls_sflight-connid
                            capacity = ls_sflight-seatsmax * 2 ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_doubled_capacity FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_doubled_capacity.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_itb_for_transform( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->get_doubled_capacity( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( msg = 'Table should not be empty' act = lt_result ).
    IF lines( lt_result ) > 0.
      DATA(ls_first_entry) = lt_result[ 1 ].
      SELECT SINGLE seatsmax FROM sflights INTO @DATA(lv_original_capacity)
        WHERE carrid = ls_first_entry-carrid AND connid = ls_first_entry-connid.
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( msg = 'Capacity should be doubled'
                                          act = ls_first_entry-capacity
                                          exp = lv_original_capacity * 2 ).
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `FOR`-Operator ermöglicht eine deklarative und kompakte Transformation von internen Tabellen, indem er eine neue Tabelle basierend auf den Elementen einer Quelltabelle erstellt. Dies ist wesentlich lesbarer und wartungsfreundlicher als traditionelle `LOOP`-Anweisungen.
keywords: FOR, VALUE, Internal Tables, Transformation, SFLIGHTS

Instructions: Berechnen Sie die Gesamtzahl der Passagiere (SEATSOCC) für alle Flüge in der SFLIGHTS-Tabelle.
hint: Verwenden Sie den `REDUCE`-Operator, um Werte zu aggregieren.
solution:
CLASS zcl_itb_reduce_sum DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS get_total_passengers
      RETURNING VALUE(rv_total) TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_itb_reduce_sum IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_total_passengers.
    SELECT seatsocc FROM sflights INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_sflights).

    rv_total = REDUCE i( INIT sum = 0
                         FOR ls_sflight IN lt_sflights
                         NEXT sum = sum + ls_sflight-seatsocc ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_total_passengers FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_total_passengers.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_itb_reduce_sum( ).
    DATA(lv_total) = lo_cut->get_total_passengers( ).

    SELECT SUM( seatsocc ) FROM sflights INTO @DATA(lv_expected_sum).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( msg = 'Total passengers should match'
                                        act = lv_total
                                        exp = lv_expected_sum ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `REDUCE`-Operator ermöglicht eine funktionale Aggregation von Werten aus internen Tabellen. Er ist prägnanter und ausdrucksstärker als eine manuelle `LOOP`- und `SUM`-Anweisung.
keywords: REDUCE, Internal Tables, Aggregation, SFLIGHTS

Instructions: Filtern Sie die SFLIGHTS-Tabelle, um nur Flüge mit einer maximalen Sitzplatzkapazität (SEATSMAX) von über 300 zu erhalten.
hint: Verwenden Sie den `FILTER`-Operator, um eine neue Tabelle basierend auf einer Bedingung zu erstellen.
solution:
CLASS zcl_itb_filter_flights DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight,
             carrid   TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid   TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate   TYPE s_date,
             seatsmax TYPE s_seatsmax,
           END OF ty_sflight.
    TYPES tt_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_large_capacity_flights
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_flights) TYPE tt_sflight.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_itb_filter_flights IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_large_capacity_flights.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, seatsmax FROM sflights INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_all_flights).

    rt_flights = FILTER #( lt_all_flights WHERE seatsmax > 300 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_filter_flights FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_filter_flights.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_itb_filter_flights( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->get_large_capacity_flights( ).

    LOOP AT lt_result INTO DATA(ls_flight).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'Flight capacity must be > 300'
                                        act = ( ls_flight-seatsmax > 300 ) ).
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_itb_table_expr DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.

             carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate TYPE s_date,
           END OF ty_sflight_key.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_info,
             carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid TYPE s_conn_id,
           END OF ty_flight_info.

    METHODS get_flight_info
      IMPORTING
        is_key        TYPE ty_sflight_key

      RAISING

CLASS zcl_itb_table_expr IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_flight_info.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate FROM sflights INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_sflights).

    DATA(ls_flight) = lt_sflights[ carrid = is_key-carrid
                                   connid = is_key-connid
                                   fldate = is_key-fldate ].
    rs_info-carrid = ls_flight-carrid.
    rs_info-connid = ls_flight-connid.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Gruppieren Sie die Flüge der SFLIGHTS-Tabelle nach Fluggesellschaft (CARRID) und ermitteln Sie für jede Gruppe die Anzahl der Flüge und die durchschnittliche maximale Sitzplatzkapazität.
hint: Verwenden Sie den `GROUP BY`-Zusatz in einer `LOOP`-Anweisung.
solution:
CLASS zcl_itb_group_by DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_grouped_flight,
             carrid        TYPE s_carr_id,
             flight_count  TYPE i,
             avg_seatsmax  TYPE decfloat16,
           END OF ty_grouped_flight.
    TYPES tt_grouped_flight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_grouped_flight WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_grouped_flight_stats
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_stats) TYPE tt_grouped_flight.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_itb_group_by IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_grouped_flight_stats.
    SELECT carrid, seatsmax FROM sflights INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_sflights).

    LOOP AT lt_sflights INTO DATA(ls_sflight) GROUP BY ls_sflight-carrid
                                              INTO DATA(ls_group_key).
      DATA(lv_flight_count) = 0.
      DATA(lv_total_seatsmax) = 0.
      LOOP AT GROUP ls_group_key INTO DATA(ls_group_member).
        lv_flight_count = lv_flight_count + 1.
        lv_total_seatsmax = lv_total_seatsmax + ls_group_member-seatsmax.
      ENDLOOP.

      APPEND VALUE #( carrid       = ls_group_key-carrid
                      flight_count = lv_flight_count
                      avg_seatsmax = COND decfloat16( WHEN lv_flight_count > 0 THEN lv_total_seatsmax / lv_flight_count ELSE 0 ) )
             TO rt_stats.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_grouped_flight_stats FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_grouped_flight_stats.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_itb_group_by( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->get_grouped_flight_stats( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( msg = 'Result table should not be empty' act = lt_result ).

    DATA(ls_lh_stats) = VALUE #( lt_result[ carrid = 'LH' ] OPTIONAL ).
    IF ls_lh_stats IS NOT INITIAL.
      SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sflights WHERE carrid = 'LH' INTO @DATA(lv_expected_count_lh).
      SELECT AVG( seatsmax ) FROM sflights WHERE carrid = 'LH' INTO @DATA(lv_expected_avg_lh).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( msg = 'LH flight count mismatch' act = ls_lh_stats-flight_count exp = lv_expected_count_lh ).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( msg = 'LH average seatsmax mismatch' act = ls_lh_stats-avg_seatsmax exp = lv_expected_avg_lh ).
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `GROUP BY`-Zusatz in `LOOP AT` ermöglicht eine leistungsstarke Gruppierung von Tabelleneinträgen direkt im ABAP-Code. Dies ist eine moderne und effiziente Art, Aggregationen und Analysen auf internen Tabellen durchzuführen, ohne temporäre Tabellen oder komplexe Schleifenkonstrukte.
keywords: GROUP BY, Internal Tables, Aggregation, SFLIGHTS, LOOP AT GROUP

Instructions: Übertragen Sie Daten von einer internen Tabelle mit SFLIGHTS-Struktur in eine andere interne Tabelle mit einer ähnlichen, aber nicht identischen Struktur, wobei nur übereinstimmende Felder kopiert werden.
hint: Verwenden Sie `MOVE-CORRESPONDING` oder den `CORRESPONDING`-Operator.
solution:
CLASS zcl_itb_corresponding DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_source,
             carrid   TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid   TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate   TYPE s_date,
             planetype TYPE s_planetye, " Additional field
             seatsmax TYPE s_seatsmax,
           END OF ty_sflight_source.
    TYPES tt_sflight_source TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight_source WITH EMPTY KEY.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_target,
             carrid   TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid   TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate   TYPE s_date,
             max_seats TYPE s_seatsmax, " Different field name
             currency TYPE s_currcode,   " Additional field
           END OF ty_sflight_target.
    TYPES tt_sflight_target TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight_target WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS transfer_flight_data
      IMPORTING
        it_source_flights TYPE tt_sflight_source
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_target_flights) TYPE tt_sflight_target.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_itb_corresponding IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD transfer_flight_data.
    rt_target_flights = CORRESPONDING #( it_source_flights MAPPING max_seats = seatsmax EXCEPT planetype ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_transfer_flight_data FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_transfer_flight_data.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_itb_corresponding( ).
    DATA(lt_source) TYPE zcl_itb_corresponding=>tt_sflight_source.
    APPEND VALUE #( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0400' fldate = '20250101' planetype = 'A320' seatsmax = 200 ) TO lt_source.
    APPEND VALUE #( carrid = 'AA' connid = '0017' fldate = '20250102' planetype = 'B747' seatsmax = 400 ) TO lt_source.

    DATA(lt_target) = lo_cut->transfer_flight_data( lt_source ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( msg = 'Target table should have 2 entries' act = lines( lt_target ) exp = 2 ).
    DATA(ls_first_target) = lt_target[ 1 ].
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( msg = 'Carrid should be LH' act = ls_first_target-carrid exp = 'LH' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( msg = 'Max seats should be 200' act = ls_first_target-max_seats exp = 200 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( msg = 'Currency should be initial' act = ls_first_target-currency ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

solution:
CLASS zcl_itb_value_for_where DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_city,
             carrid   TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid   TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate   TYPE s_date,

      RETURNING VALUE(rt_flights) TYPE tt_sflight_city.

CLASS zcl_itb_value_for_where IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_frankfurt_newyork_flights.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, cityfrom, cityto FROM sflights INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_all_flights).

    rt_flights = VALUE #(
      FOR ls_flight IN lt_all_flights WHERE ( cityfrom = 'FRANKFURT' AND cityto = 'NEW YORK' )
      ( ls_flight )
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_flight_descriptions FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_flight_descriptions.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_itb_string_template( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->get_flight_descriptions( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( msg = 'Result table should not be empty' act = lt_result ).
    IF lines( lt_result ) > 0.
      DATA(ls_first_desc) = lt_result[ 1 ].
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( msg = 'Description should not be empty' act = ls_first_desc-description ).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'Description should contain "Flug"' act = ( CONTAINS( val = ls_first_desc-description sub = 'Flug' ) ) ).
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: String-Templates (`|...|`) bieten eine moderne und intuitive Möglichkeit, Strings zu formatieren und Variablen direkt einzubetten. In Kombination mit dem `FOR`-Operator können so schnell und lesbar formatierte Daten in internen Tabellen erzeugt werden, was die String-Verkettung mit `&&` oder `CONCATENATE` überflüssig macht.
keywords: String Templates, FOR, Internal Tables, Formatting, SFLIGHTS
